text: `parseDigits` returns `NaN` for a string with no parseable digits: `parseInt(str, 10)` is `NaN`, so it falls into the loop, which appends nothing (no Han decimal chars, no code points in any of the `numberingSystemsUTF16` ranges), and it ends with `parseInt("", 10)`, i.e. `NaN`.

It returns `[matches, {}]` — i.e. a two-element array whose first element is the failed `String.prototype.match` result (`null`) and whose second element is an empty object. (On success it returns `[matches, all]`, where `all` holds the deserialized token values.)
`run` catches the exception, logs it with `console.error(e)`, and returns the string `"[error]"`.

Nothing — it just leaves it. Each `example(...)` call pushes a `<tr>` HTML string onto `examples`; after all the calls, `demo` joins that array (`examples.join("")`) into the page HTML and assigns the result to `document.body.innerHTML`. The array itself is neither cleared nor reused.
`latn` (Latin digits) — `digitRegex` uses `numberingSystems[numberingSystem || "latn"]`, and `latn` maps to `\d`.
It sets the internal `defaultZone` variable to `null` (it does not call `normalizeZone`), so the `Settings.defaultZone` getter subsequently returns `LocalZone.instance`.

It returns a `FixedOffsetZone` built from the matched offset: `zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)`. (If `matches.Z` is undefined it checks `matches.z` and returns `IANAZone.create(matches.z)`, otherwise `null`.)
